contents.name: Finite-field Hall spectrum generator and its conventions

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the complete Hall product definition in Section 2.1 and the stability and phase conventions in Section 4.4.
source_review.supports: Sections 2.1 and 4.4 define the finitary Hall convolution, subobject flags, stability phases, semistability, and the HN property used to formulate the ordered generator.
source_review.limitations: The local definition states the exact finite-field quiver and Euler/skew conventions; this survey does not replace the inspected local integration theorem or assert a physical state-space interpretation.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the full Lemma 4.2 statement and proof and the wall-crossing consequence in Sections 4.5–4.6.
source_review.supports: The proof expands the ordered product into flags and uses existence and uniqueness of HN filtrations to count each object exactly once; the hereditary integration map sends the identity to a completed quantum-torus identity.
source_review.limitations: The local proposition uses the exact finite-quiver root theorem and its subobject-first Euler/skew normalizations. Bridgeland's later motivic and CY3 constructions are not substituted for those hypotheses.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the full scope discussion in Section 3.5, including the CY3 Hall integration map, motivic vanishing-cycle discussion, orientation-data issue, and the separate semiclassical DT construction.
source_review.supports: Section 3.5 distinguishes the hereditary finite-field integration from motivic/CY3 integration and identifies orientation data and the sign/Behrend-function conditions as additional inputs.
source_review.limitations: The source does not provide a physical protected-state dictionary; the local item defines that comparison as a separate required input and asserts no such identification.

sources.title: Markus Reineke, The Harder–Narasimhan system in quantum groups and cohomology of quiver moduli
sources.locator: Full 22-page paper; PDF Section 2, especially Proposition 2.5, and Section 4, especially Lemma 4.7, Proposition 4.8, and Theorem 4.9.
sources.reading_extent: Read the complete relevant stability, HN existence/uniqueness, Hall multiplication, HN-stratum, and recursive-factorization passages and their stated proofs.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected Section 2 definitions of slope stability and HN filtrations and the full induction proof of Proposition 2.5.
source_review.supports: The paper independently develops finite-dimensional quiver representations and proves HN existence and uniqueness by maximal-slope subobjects.
source_review.limitations: Its stability convention is a rational slope from a linear weight, not the arbitrary upper-half-plane central charge used here; the local theorem's hypotheses and proof are stated independently.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected the Hall product and filtration formula in Section 4 and the HN-stratum recursion through Theorem 4.9.
source_review.supports: The HN strata partition each representation variety, and the Hall convolution counts filtrations; the ordered HN system is built by summing those strata.
source_review.limitations: Reineke uses a twisted Kapranov Hall algebra and slope stability. The finite-field Euler/skew maps, upper-half-plane charge convention, and BPS boundary are supplied or qualified separately.
